FINDINGS intent PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py

  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.95
  reachability: routine
  claim: The stated avoidance of O(n) database I/O for canvas-version deletion is not achieved because indexed Peewee query access still issues a query for every version beyond the retention limit.
  evidence: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py:35-36 iterates `user_canvas_version[i]`; each indexed query access requires an offset/limit fetch, before the new batch delete at :38.
  fix: Materialize the IDs in one query before calling `delete_by_ids`.
- path: api/apps/api_app.py
  line: 636
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.92
  reachability: routine
  claim: The document-delete path still performs a per-document database lookup, so the body’s claim to avoid O(n) database I/O is only partially implemented.
  evidence: api/apps/api_app.py:636 batch-loads documents, but the loop at :641-646 calls `DocumentService.get_tenant_id` once per ID; api/db/services/document_service.py:215-225 defines that call as a database select/join.
  fix: Include the required tenant information in the batch lookup or retrieve it in a single bulk query.

FINDINGS placement PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/db/services/document_service.py
  line: 339
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: The new batch lookup must return an empty collection for no matches, since its caller unconditionally treats its result as a collection.
  evidence: DocumentService.get_doc_ids_by_doc_names returns None when no names match (api/db/services/document_service.py:337-340), while document_rm immediately evaluates `doc_id not in doc_ids` for supplied IDs (api/apps/api_app.py:618-621); therefore a delete request containing only doc_ids, or an unknown name plus a valid ID, raises TypeError.
  fix: Return an empty list when the query finds no documents.

FINDINGS backcompat PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/apps/api_app.py
  line: 618
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: ID-only document deletion requests now fail because an empty name lookup returns `None` before IDs are merged.
  detail: Cached/current frontend callers send `{doc_ids: [...]}` without `doc_names`; the new service returns `None` for the implicit empty name list, so `if doc_id not in doc_ids` raises and the endpoint returns a server error instead of deleting the requested document. The merged identifier collection must tolerate absent or unmatched names as empty while preserving ID-only deletion.
  evidence: api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 returns `None` for no matches; api/apps/api_app.py:618-621 then performs containment and append; web/src/hooks/document-hooks.ts:421 sends only `doc_ids`.
  fix: Initialize or normalize the name-resolution result to an empty collection before merging explicit IDs.
- path: api/apps/api_app.py
  line: 618
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.96
  reachability: routine
  claim: Name-based deletion now expands one requested name into every globally matching document, allowing a single delete request to remove unrelated same-named documents.
  detail: Document names are not unique and the new global `IN` query returns every matching row, whereas the prior lookup selected only one ID per supplied name; the deletion loop then removes each returned document without constraining it to the API token's tenant. A common filename such as `README.md` can therefore delete multiple tenants' documents after deployment. Name deletion must resolve only the caller's intended document set and must not silently expand ambiguous names.
  evidence: api/db/db_models.py:615-644 defines `Document.name` as a non-unique indexed field; api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 selects all rows with matching names; api/apps/api_app.py:618 and :641-655 delete every resulting ID without tenant filtering.
  fix: Scope name resolution to the authenticated tenant and reject or otherwise safely handle ambiguous names.

FINDINGS simplicity PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py
  line: 35
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P2
  confidence: 0.98
  reachability: routine
  claim: The version-pruning path still performs one database query per obsolete version, defeating the stated bulk-delete performance goal.
  detail: Peewee query indexing at `user_canvas_version[i]` applies a per-index LIMIT/OFFSET query, so canvases with many saved versions issue O(n) reads before the single bulk delete; the pruning path should fetch all obsolete IDs in one query before deleting them.
  evidence: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py:32 builds a lazy ordered query; :35-36 repeatedly call `.count()` and index that query once per version, before :38 performs the one batch deletion.
  fix: Iterate a single offset ID-select query (or use a delete subquery) rather than indexing the query in a loop.
- path: api/db/services/document_service.py
  line: 339
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: The new plural lookup returns `None` for an empty result even though its caller unconditionally treats it as a list, so document-ID-only deletes now fail before processing any supplied IDs.
  evidence: api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 returns `None` when `doc_names` is absent or has no match; api/apps/api_app.py:618 passes the optional `doc_names`, then :619-621 evaluates membership and `.append()` on that result for every supplied `doc_id`.
  fix: Return an empty list from the plural lookup when no names match.
- path: api/db/services/document_service.py
  line: 336
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P3
  confidence: 0.92
  reachability: plausible
  claim: Resolving delete names without tenant scope broadens a name delete to every document with that name, including documents owned by other tenants.
  evidence: api/apps/api_app.py:615 obtains the API token tenant but api/db/services/document_service.py:335-336 filters only `Document.name`; api/db/db_models.py:615-638 defines no global uniqueness constraint on document names, while api/apps/document_app.py:166 only rejects duplicates within one knowledgebase.
  fix: Ensure name-based deletion resolution is constrained to the authenticated tenant.

FINDINGS baseline PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/apps/api_app.py
  line: 618
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: The new name lookup returns `None` rather than an empty collection, breaking valid ID-only document deletion requests.
  detail: When `doc_names` is omitted or has no matches, `get_doc_ids_by_doc_names([])` returns `None`; the subsequent membership test against `doc_ids` raises `TypeError`, which the route converts to a server error before supplied `doc_ids` can be processed. The lookup result must remain iterable so either identifier form can be used independently.
  evidence: api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 returns bare `None` for an empty query; api/apps/api_app.py:618-621 immediately performs `doc_id not in doc_ids` and `append`, while the previous list-comprehension always produced a list.
  fix: Return an empty list for no matching names.
- path: api/db/services/document_service.py
  line: 336
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P1
  confidence: 0.96
  reachability: plausible
  claim: Name-based deletion is not tenant-scoped, so the new bulk lookup can delete every tenant's document sharing a requested filename.
  detail: `Document.name` is indexed but not unique, and this query selects all matching IDs without joining/filtering by the authenticated token's tenant; `document_rm` then iterates every returned ID and replaces the token tenant with each document's tenant before removing it. Thus a valid tenant token deleting a common name such as `report.pdf` can remove matching documents owned by other tenants. Name resolution for this endpoint must be constrained to documents authorized for the caller.
  evidence: api/db/db_models.py:615-649 defines `Document.name` without a uniqueness or tenant constraint; api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 filters only by name; api/apps/api_app.py:610-615 obtains the token tenant, then api/apps/api_app.py:641-658 deletes each matched document after `get_tenant_id`. Shared machinery checked: `@DB.connection_context()` on the lookup and deletion service methods does not impose authorization.
  fix: Scope the bulk lookup and subsequent deletion set to the authenticated tenant's knowledgebases.
- path: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py
  line: 36
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P2
  confidence: 0.9
  reachability: routine
  claim: The canvas-version path still performs O(n) database reads, so the claimed elimination of O(n) DB I/O is not achieved.
  detail: Once a canvas has more than 20 versions, each positional `user_canvas_version[i]` fetches a row to obtain its ID before the eventual bulk delete, yielding one indexed query per obsolete version. The pruning path must obtain the obsolete IDs as a set/stream rather than individually indexing the query.
  evidence: api/db/services/user_canvas_version.py:32-38 counts the query and then indexes it once for every value in `range(20, count)`; only the final delete is batched through api/db/services/common_service.py:267-275.
  fix: Retrieve the obsolete IDs with one ID-only query before calling `delete_by_ids`.

FINDINGS security-tenancy PR#6553 @705123406ec7cd5eb1f9be26f6c5c31357aeffc9
- path: api/db/services/document_service.py
  line: 336
  side: RIGHT
  severity: P0
  confidence: 0.99
  reachability: routine
  claim: Bulk document-name resolution must be tenant-scoped; the new global lookup causes delete-by-name requests to delete every same-named document belonging to other tenants.
  detail: The authenticated tenant is read but never supplied to the new query, which returns all IDs matching globally non-unique names rather than the previous helper's single row; common filenames across tenants therefore enter the deletion loop, which replaces the caller tenant with each document's owning tenant and removes that tenant's database, search-index, file, and storage records. Every selected document must be authorized against the API token's tenant before deletion.
  evidence: api/apps/api_app.py:609-618 authenticates and obtains the caller tenant but calls the lookup with names only; api/db/services/document_service.py:333-340 filters solely on Document.name and returns every match; api/db/db_models.py:615-624 defines name as a non-unique index, while api/apps/document_app.py:166-168 only prevents duplicates within one knowledgebase; api/apps/api_app.py:636-660 iterates every returned ID, overwrites tenant_id from that document, and deletes it.
  fix: Restrict name resolution and the final deletion set to documents authorized for the authenticated tenant.

  claim: Bulk name resolution allows an authenticated caller to delete every same-named document across tenants.
  detail: `Document.name` is not unique, and the new query returns every global match without filtering by the API token tenant; the route then derives each matched document's owner and deletes its database, search, file-link, and storage state, so a common filename can erase other tenants' documents.
  evidence: api/db/db_models.py:615-639; api/db/services/document_service.py:102-116,215-224,333-340; api/apps/api_app.py:609-618,636-661
